Biophysical properties: Normal.

Liquor:- Adequate liquor volume.

Placenta:- Showing grade `___ ’ maturity with clear margins and Retroplacental areas. Lower end of placenta is seen extending within lower uterine segment.

 

Fetal parameters:- BPD = ___ mm  = ___ weeks ___ days,   HC = ___ mm = ___ weeks ___ days

                                      FL    = ___ mm  = ___ weeks ___ days,   AC = ___ mm = ___ weeks ___ days

Estimated fetal weight:- ______________ gms ± 15% (approx).  LMP (  ______________ ).

Gestational Age by LMP :- ______ weeks  ______ days.

 

                                                                  ANATOMICAL SCAN:

SKULL & BRAIN:- Cranial outline apparently intact. Brain parenchyma apparently normal. Both lateral ventricles normal and symmetrical with normal choroid plexus – interatrial diameter: 07-08 mm (normal). Cavum septum pellucidum; midbrain; thalami; cerebellum unremarkable – cisterna magna well preserved. Cranio-vertebral junction apparently unremarkable.

 

SPINE:- Cervical; dorsal and lumbo-sacral spine apparently unremarkable – showing normal epiphyses.

 

FACE:- Orbit with eyeball; nose as well as mandible unremarkable – palate visible and apparently intact. Neck shows no obvious abnormality.

 

THORAX:- Lungs collapsed – not echogenic. No pleural effusion seen. Cardiac impression apparently normal – interventricular septum and left ventricular outflow tract apparently intact. Diaphragm intact (at present).

 

ABDOMEN:- Liver and portal vein unremarkable. Stomach well distended with fluid. Both kidneys just visible – showing mildly dilated renal pelvis [diameter: ______   mm]. Urinary bladder partially distended. Bowels collapsed and echogenic.

 

EXTREMITIES:- Both upper and lower extremities apparently unremarkable with normal long bones – fingers well visible.

 

(Not all congenital anomalies could be detected in single routine study – also overall detection rate is 70-80% of all anomalies).

 

Lower Uterine segment, Internal Os and Cervical canal appear normal.  Cervix is normal in length.

* Adequate liquor.

Disclaimer :

Fetal congenital anomalies cannot be ruled out completely by sonography alone. It also dependents on gestational age, fetal position during scan, amniotic fluid volume & acoustic window. Best scanned between 18-25 weeks of gestation.

Overall detection rate of major congenital abnormalities are around 70 %. Some abnormalities are seen only in 3rd trimester. Thus, not detectable at this stage.

This is a screening test for structural abnormalities. It does not confirm/exclude chromosomal or functional abnormalities in fetus.

Fetal gender has neither been detected nor disclosed. 

“Normal” means structurally normal for the gestation within reasonable expectations for available for available technology.

Uterine & adnexal abnormality is best viewed in 1st trimester scan.

Fetal gestational age correlated well with sonographic parameters if it is done before 26 weeks

{with ± 1 week variation} & after 26 weeks {with ± 2-3 weeks variation.
